{{Quote|Suddenly, the shaman took one of the boy's totems, which he had been wearing around his neck, and held it up. The boy stood up and, throwing his head back, swallowed the small, beaded object, string and all. I was certain something so large would cause him to choke, or would get stuck in his digestive tract. But according to the shaman, they do this all the time, and with the passing of the totem, so, too, passes the disease.|Senior Anthropologist Mammon Hoole, on a Kurtzen healing ceremony|<ref name="The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref>}}
An ailing [[Kurtzen]] '''boy''' was the subject of a healing ceremony witnessed by the [[Shi'ido]] [[Senior Anthropologist]] [[Mammon Hoole]] during his fieldwork on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Bakura/Legends|Bakura]]. To heal the boy, a [[Unidentified Kurtzen shaman|shaman]] passed a [[Life trinket|totem]] through the boy's throat. Although Hoole feared the trinket would cause the [[Youngling/Legends|boy]] to choke, it went down safely. The [[Shaman/Legends|shaman]] reported that once the totem passed, the boy's sickness would pass as well. Hoole's description of the event was later added to the entry on the Kurtzen [[Species/Legends|species]] in ''[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'', published during the regime of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]].
